title: The Supermarket That Sold Expired Meat for 30 Years
hook: A major grocery chain systematically repackaged expired meat and sold it as fresh—until a single whistleblower ended the scheme.
why_this_can_go_viral: Extreme disgust and betrayal—everyone shops at grocery stores, making the threat personal and shareable.

title: The Bank That Shortened Your Mortgage by 10 Years—Secretly
hook: A global bank quietly manipulated interest calculations on millions of loans, stealing billions in hidden fees.
why_this_can_go_viral: Financial betrayal triggers outrage—viewers will feel personally targeted and share to warn others.

title: The Startup That Used Prison Labor to Build Its Product
hook: A trendy tech startup outsourced assembly to a prison program paying 20 cents an hour—and branded it as 'artisanal'.
why_this_can_go_viral: Moral outrage plus hidden labor supply chain—people love exposing fake ethical brands.

title: The Company That Bought a Patent Just to Kill a Cure
hook: A pharmaceutical giant acquired a breakthrough treatment for a rare disease and immediately buried it to protect existing drug sales.
why_this_can_go_viral: Life-or-death injustice—everyone fears hidden cures, and the villain is a classic corporate monster.

title: The Hotel Chain That Secretly Recorded Guests for Blackmail
hook: A luxury hotel network hid cameras in rooms and used the footage to extort high-profile guests into silence.
why_this_can_go_viral: Extreme violation of privacy—everyone stays in hotels, making the threat universal and deeply unsettling.

title: The Chocolate Company That Mixed Sawdust Into Your Bar
hook: A beloved brand bulked up its chocolate with cheap wood fiber for decades, hiding it behind 'fiber' labels.
why_this_can_go_viral: Disgust and nostalgia—people love sharing 'I can't believe I ate that' stories with friends.

title: The Meat Plant That Sold Horse as Beef for 20 Years
hook: An abattoir replaced expensive beef with horse meat across Europe—and no one noticed until a random DNA test.
why_this_can_go_viral: Gross-out factor plus global scandal—people will immediately check their burgers and share the shock.

title: The CEO Who Faked His Own Kidnapping to Hide Losses
hook: A startup founder staged his own abduction to delay an audit that would expose $200 million in missing investor funds.
why_this_can_go_viral: Audacious lie—people love true-crime business stories that feel like movie plots.

title: The Oil Company That Paid Bounties for Whistleblower Deaths
hook: A petroleum giant secretly funded a program to silence workers who exposed pipeline leaks—with lethal force.
why_this_can_go_viral: Extreme darkness and human cost—shock value plus moral fury drive massive shares.

title: The Insurance Company That Denied Claims with a Dice Roll
hook: A claims adjuster revealed that his firm used a literal algorithm that randomly rejected 30% of valid claims to save cash.
why_this_can_go_viral: Everyone hates insurance—this confirms the worst suspicions and triggers massive anger shares.

title: The Factory That Faked Safety Inspections for 15 Years
hook: A toy manufacturer bribed inspectors to sign off on toxic paint—leading to thousands of child poisonings before discovery.
why_this_can_go_viral: Children at risk—parents will share furiously, and the villain is a faceless corporation.

title: The Rival Who Hired Actors to Pose as Your Customers
hook: A startup paid actors to file fake complaints against a competitor, triggering a regulatory shutdown that destroyed the business.
why_this_can_go_viral: Dirty tactics feel like a thriller—small business owners especially will empathize and share.

title: The Ad Agency That Invented a Disease to Sell a Drug
hook: A marketing firm created a fake medical condition, hired fake doctors, and convinced millions they needed treatment for nothing.
why_this_can_go_viral: Medical manipulation triggers deep distrust—people love exposing how they've been tricked into buying sickness.

title: The Car Company That Built a Death Trap—Then Denied It
hook: An automaker discovered a fatal brake flaw during testing but shipped the cars anyway, then deleted all internal emails.
why_this_can_go_viral: Death on the road—every driver feels vulnerable, and the cover-up adds fuel to outrage.

title: The Monopoly That Made You Pay Rent for Parking Spaces
hook: A company bought 90% of downtown parking lots in 50 cities, then doubled prices overnight—and no one could stop them.
why_this_can_go_viral: Relatable frustration—every city driver hates parking fees, and the hidden monopoly story fuels rage.

title: The Software That Forced Employees to Quit—Then Kept Their Pay
hook: A retail chain used an algorithm to push workers into resigning, then continued collecting their government subsidies for months.
why_this_can_go_viral: Workers' rights violation—will resonate with gig economy and retail workers, driving mass shares.

title: The Pharma Exec Who Sold Fake Medicine to Save Face
hook: A pharmaceutical executive ordered factory workers to substitute expensive ingredients with chalk—after a failed profit quarter.
why_this_can_go_viral: Health betrayal—everyone takes medicine, and the idea of being sold chalk is viscerally shocking.

title: The Coffee House Chain That Paid Hobos to Deter Customers
hook: A rival coffee brand paid homeless individuals to camp outside a competitor's shops, creating a safety panic that killed foot traffic.
why_this_can_go_viral: Cruelty and creativity shock—people will share the sheer audacity of the tactic.

title: The Mining Company That Buried a Town's Water Supply
hook: A mining operation illegally dumped toxic runoff into an aquifer, poisoning an entire town—then bought the silence of every resident.
why_this_can_go_viral: Environmental justice story with a corporate villain—activists and locals will fuel massive reach.

title: The Recruiter Who Sold Candidates' Secrets to Their Rivals
hook: A headhunting agency secretly shared salaray data and personal weaknesses of job applicants with their current employers to weaken leverage.
why_this_can_go_viral: Career paranoia—anyone who has job-hunted will feel exposed and share to warn peers.

title: The Sugar Lobby That Paid Scientists to Blame Fat for 30 Years
hook: The sugar industry secretly funded top nutrition researchers to publish papers demonizing fat, while hiding sugar's role in obesity.
why_this_can_go_viral: Decades of deception—everyone is affected by diet, and the 'they lied to us' narrative is explosively shareable.

title: The Founder Who Simulated His Own App Launch—Fooled Everyone
hook: A startup CEO created a fake viral launch video, hired bots to fake downloads, and duped VCs into a $50 million investment.
why_this_can_go_viral: Tech bubble skepticism—everyone loves a story about faking it until you make it, then getting caught.

title: The Water Bottler That Drained a Village Dry—Then Sold It Back
hook: A beverage corporation bought the rights to a village's aquifer, pumped it dry, then sold bottled water to the same villagers at 100x the cost.
why_this_can_go_viral: Global injustice—water is a universal right, and the exploitation story triggers deep empathy and anger.

title: The Supply Chain Middleman Who Added 500% to Your Medicine
hook: A hidden broker bought up generic drug supplies, created artificial shortages, then resold them at massive markups to hospitals.
why_this_can_go_viral: Healthcare cost crisis—everyone pays for medicine, and exposing hidden middlemen feeds righteous anger.
